item.title: AMD Unveils New Products in Pursuit of $2 Trillion Market
item.description: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. announced a raft of new products for data centers that it said will outperform those from rival Nvidia Corp., aiming to make gains in a booming market for artificial intelligence computing.

item.title: Heat Worries US Wheat Farmers Just as Crop Prices Are Surging
item.description: For farmers in North Dakota surveying their wheat as harvest closes in, scorching heat is threatening yields just as crop prices rise to a three-year high.

item.title: Magnificent 7 Loses $767 Billion as AI Skeptics Dump Tech Stocks
item.description: The Magnificent Seven group of megacap technology stocks is on track for its biggest one-day drop since the tariff tantrum in April 2025 as results from Alphabet Inc. and Tesla Inc. are casting doubt on the durability of the artificial intelligence trade that has powered the stock market for more than three years.

item.title: Microsoft Replacing OpenAI Image AI Models in Powerpoint, Bing
item.description: Microsoft Corp. is replacing OpenAI’s image-generating models with its own technology in popular products like PowerPoint and Bing.

item.title: BlackRock’s GIP Eyes Bundling Fund Stakes in Securitization Deal
item.description: BlackRock Inc.’s Global Infrastructure Partners LP has been in discussions with investors to sell bonds backed by stakes in some of its private capital funds, joining a growing list of asset managers exploring ways to bolster returns on their holdings.

item.title: NYC’s Former HSBC Tower Seeks More Than $800 Million in Sale
item.description: A Manhattan office tower where Amazon.com Inc. has offices is going up for sale.

item.title: Chocolate Maker Lindt Faces US Lawsuit Over Child Labor Allegations
item.description: Lindt & Spruengli AG has been sued by an activist law firm in the US which alleges the Swiss chocolate maker is falsely promoting its efforts to battle child labor in Ghana and the Ivory Coast from where it sources cocoa.

item.title: Drone Navigation Firms Seek New Ways Past Warzone Jamming
item.description: GPS spoofing and other countermeasures meant to knock drones from the skies over battlefields are giving rise to novel navigation systems that will work even in the face of intense jamming.

item.title: How Leveraged Exchange-Traded Funds Are Suddenly Everywhere
item.description: On this episode of Trillions, we discuss what’s fueling the boom and how these exchange-traded funds work in today’s market.

item.title: Thermo Fisher Rises as Instrument Demand Recovery Lifts Outlook
item.description: Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc. raised its revenue forecast after stronger-than-expected spending by biotech and pharma customers and a rebound in laboratory instrument demand helped pushed second-quarter sales past expectations. Shares jumped.

item.title: The Worrying Signal Embedded in the Momentum Selloff
item.description: A loss of market leadership.

item.title: Ireland Says Alumina Probe Finds No Proof of Russia Weapons Link
item.description: An investigation into alumina exports from Ireland to Russia has not found conclusive evidence linking a production plant to the manufacture of weapons in Russia, Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin said.

item.title: Blackstone Leads $400 Million Private Loan For HVAC Firm Buyout
item.description: Blackstone Inc. led a roughly $400 million deal to support the buyout of Integra Testing Services by Harvest Partners LP, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: ECB Presents 10 Design Options for New Euro-Area Banknotes
item.description: The European Central Bank offered a first glimpse of designs for a new generation of euro banknotes, just as it prepares to begin a trial of the digital version of the currency.

item.title: Alphabet’s Future Spending Commitments Soar to $811 Billion
item.description: Alphabet Inc.’s Google had $811 billion in contracted future spending commitments at the end of June, up nearly $500 billion from just three months earlier.

item.title: Dollar Jumps on Haven Flows as Middle East War Intensifies
item.description: The dollar got a boost Thursday from haven flows as the war in the Middle East intensified, pushing oil prices above $100 a barrel.

item.title: Russia Says Its Black Sea Waters Not Safe for Ships Amid Attacks
item.description: Russia warned that it was unsafe to navigate in its Black Sea waters after Ukraine ramped up attacks on ships.

item.title: ECB Officials Are Ready to Raise Interest Rates in September
item.description: European Central Bank officials are prepared to raise borrowing costs in September unless the euro-zone inflation outlook improves markedly, people familiar with the situation said.

item.title: Dow Says Iran War Could Boost Guidance as Supply Chain Shielded
item.description: Dow Inc. said that persistent tensions in the Middle East could help raise prices for plastics and packaging without lifting its material costs, padding profits and offering upside to the group’s third-quarter guidance.

item.title: World Bank Estimates Quakes Cost Venezuela $20 Billion in Damage
item.description: The twin earthquakes that hit Venezuela last month may have caused $19.6 billion in physical damage to buildings and infrastructure, or about 18% of gross domestic product, according to a preliminary assessment by the World Bank.

item.title: Alphabet Falls as $205 Billion Spending Plan Fuels AI Cost Fear
item.description: Alphabet Inc. raised its capital spending forecast to as much as $205 billion this year, reigniting concerns about a lack of fiscal discipline in the race to dominate artificial intelligence.

item.title: How Trump Plans to Maintain His Tariff Wall
item.description: From the start of his second term, US President Donald Trump made clear he would put tariffs at the center of US economic policy. When the Supreme Court invalidated sweeping import duties he’d imposed citing emergency powers, he used a different provision, Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974, to set a flat 10% levy on imports. Such tariffs are time-limited, however, and Trump’s expire on July 24.

item.title: Brazil Races to Safeguard $1.8 Billion of Meat Exports to EU
item.description: Brazil is rushing to avoid a ban on its animal product shipments to the European Union, with more than $1.8 billion of trade from the world’s top beef and poultry exporter at risk.

item.title: Lagarde Says She’s Staying at the ECB at Least Until Year End
item.description: President Christine Lagarde said she doesn’t want to be pinned down on the timing of her exit from the European Central Bank, but it won’t be before the end of this year.

item.title: BlackRock Says Focus on Credit Income in a Volatile Market
item.description: BlackRock Inc. is making the case for European corporate bonds even though their spread is close to the tightest on record.

item.title: Three Crude Supertankers Slip Out Through the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Three very large crude carriers hauling about 6 million barrels of crude slipped out of the Persian Gulf via the Strait of Hormuz in the past 24 hours, running the gauntlet of potential attack by Iran.

item.title: US Initial Jobless Claims Fall to Lowest Level Since 1969
item.description: First-time applications for US unemployment benefits fell last week to the lowest level since 1969, signaling layoffs remain muted in a stable labor market.

item.title: Spain’s Cuerpo Expects Economy to Continue Resisting Iran War
item.description: Spanish Economy Minister Carlos Cuerpo said he expects the country to shrug off the impact of the Iran war and post further strong expansion.

item.title: The Most Fundamental Macro Risk Is Back: MacroScope
item.description: Rising inflation volatility is set to trigger earnings disappointments, wider credit spreads and more variability in stock and bond prices.
